newsitem.title: UK: Frankfurt and London stocks hit new highs.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt and London stocks hit new highs.

text.p: Leading German and British stocks hit fresh highs on Monday, boosted by Wall Street's strong close last week as the U.S. market celebrated positive inflation data.

By 1100 GMT Frankfurt's DAX index was up 1.3 percent -- about 30 points above its previous peak, set on Friday. Dealers said gains were underpinned by the firmer dollar -- which made German exports more attractive.

London stocks were about four points up on their Friday record high but down from the Monday opening peak of 3,980.8 as late morning trade saw the rally stall. Dealers said cautious investors were sitting back to see if Wall Street would repeat its 1.15 percent rise of Friday, when the Dow closed at a record 5,838.52 as treasuries powered ahead.

"It was a very predictable move. We saw a squeeze up on the opening after Friday's euphoria and then it came back. It feels like it will still go to 4,000 this week but we will have to have Wall Street very strong to get it there," said one trader.
Dealers were sceptical the psychological 4,000 level could be passed on Monday, despite talk that investment funds were poised to pump more liquidity into the market.

"I think we would have to wait for more significant corporate news before that comes. Volumes weren't that exciting on Friday. Also, there are some suspicions about whether Wall Street can hold those gains," one said.
The Paris bourse started flat, following its 3.77 percent gain last week, but recovered in mid-morning to trade in positive territory. Traders said it was pausing for breath amid profit-taking.

On the Milan bourse, Olivetti shares were automatically suspended after plunging 10 percent following news that the crisis-hit Italian information technology group's chief executive was under preliminary investigation by magistrates.
On foreign exchange markets, the dollar was stuck in a tight range though slightly firmer than Friday's closing levels. Analysts said there was little likely to stir the market up.
With Tokyo out overnight for a market holiday, early volume was light and traders reckoned there was a good chance the dollar could give up some of its recent gains during the course of the week.
Support lent by the Iraq crisis was fading, they said, and the view was growing that U.S. interest rates would be left unchanged at the September 24 meeting of the Federal Open Markets Committee.

"The dollar is likely to struggle this week to hold on to its recent gains," said Klaus Baader, currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "Most importantly, interest rate support is waning." Buoyant oil prices eased on Monday after Iraq appeared to defuse a military standoff with Washington by suspending attacks on U.S. warplanes patrolling Iraqi no fly zones.

November futures for international benchmark North Sea Brent blend traded down 70 cents at $22.43 a barrel shortly after opening in London. Brent for October hit a five-year post Gulf War peak at $24.39 a barrel last Thursday after Iraq fired missiles at U.S. planes and Washington sent more weaponry to the region.
CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5125 marks and 110.43 yen compared with late Friday's 1.5112 marks and 110.32 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1100 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares had risen 6.3 points to 3,974.2.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index gained 7.74 to 2,088.11.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 31.69 at 2,627.65.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixes at $382.65 compared with Friday's London close of $383.10. Silver was also weaker at $5.04.
